newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Mixed fortunes for European truck makers.
newsitem.headline: Mixed fortunes for European truck makers.

text.p: Leading European truck makers Mercedes-Benz AG and Scania reported strong 1996 sales Friday but another major manufacturer, Volvo, had a miserable year due to plunging U.S. sales.

Mercedes truck unit chief Kurt Lauk said at the Brussels truck show that 1996 sales climbed to 348,200 units from 320,100, helped by the company's light trucks and vans, and were likely to rise above 350,000 in 1997.
Scania said its share of the market in Western Europe rose to 15.5 percent between January and November 1996 from 14.5 percent a year earlier.
But fellow Swedish firm Volvo said 1996 sales dived 17 percent to 63,682 due to a fall in North and Latin American sales.
Volvo said that in North America it sold 16,855 trucks last year, down 38 percent from 27,092 in 1995. In Latin America sales fell 36 percent to 4,982 trucks from 7,798 the previous year.

At Mercedes' truck unit revenue slipped to 31.5 million marks ($19.7 million) from 31.6 million despite the higher sales. But Lauk said the unit was positioned for higher profits and that by the end of the decade it would be able to make a profit in all its operations.
He said Mercedes had been hit especially hard by weak European demand for heavy trucks and had seen its market share slip in that sector in recent years, analysts said.
